subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>
To: Jack Reynolds <jack.reynolds@finbot.ai>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.in>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Hi Jack / Sana — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points (what you told us):
- Monthly inference spend is spiking (~$120k/month) as you scale from 10k -> 60k daily requests.
- Latency-sensitive features (session-based chat & realtime scoring) need p95 < 200ms but current endpoints struggle.
- Quality regressions when trying smaller models; team needs predictable unit economics before switching.

Current stack:
- Model: mix of Llama-2 13B (quantized) for embeddings and a hosted 70B for chat fallback.
- Serving: managed endpoints with autoscale (cloud vendor), minimal batching enabled.
- Monitoring: basic logs + Prometheus metrics; no token-level cost breakdown yet.

Success criteria for an evaluation:
- Reduce per-request inference cost by >= 30% without >2% drop in key QA metrics.
- Maintain p95 latency <= 200ms for chat use case at production traffic patterns.
- Clear migration path that preserves data isolation and auditability.

What we propose next:
1) Technical deep-dive (1 hour) with your infra/ML Eng team to scope benchmarking and identify compatible model variants. Suggested slots: Thu 2/26 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 2/27 11:00–12:00 PT.
2) Share our lightweight cost-model template (attached) — please fill in QPS, avg tokens in/out, current batch sizes.
3) Small pilot: 1-week throughput/latency benchmark on a representative workload (we run side-by-side) + evaluation on your eval set.

Open items we flagged on the call:
- Quantization: you said you’re open to int8/4-bit but need to know expected quality delta.
- Batching/caching: currently minimal; you’re open to prefix/KV caching if it preserves session semantics.
- Security: you requested SOC2 evidence — attached baseline doc; we’ll route security questionnaire to our trust team if needed.

Next steps for this thread: pick a deep-dive slot, complete the attached cost-model, and I’ll loop Ben (cc’d) to prepare benchmarking plan.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.in | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: redwood_inference_cost_model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
Attachment: security_baseline.pdf (summary, 6 pages)
From: Jack Reynolds <jack.reynolds@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@finbot.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Marissa — great summary, thanks. Confirming a few specifics from our side so your team can size things appropriately: 

Additional context / numbers:
- Current monthly spend: ~$120k across inference + hosting. Token-based cost is ~60% of that.
- Traffic profile: 10k daily active -> projected 60k in next 6 months; peak concurrent qps ~450 for chat scoring.
- Avg prompt length: 220 tokens in, 80 tokens out for chat; reranker calls are shorter (~50 tokens total).

Batching & caching:
- We currently have minimal batching enabled (max batch size 8) because of latency concerns. Ideally we’d increase batching dynamically for non-realtime routes.
- Open to prefix caching for session-based flows if it doesn’t break personalization.

Quantization:
- Engineering team is willing to test int8 and 4-bit variants if we can get concrete latency/cost tradeoffs and a controlled A/B to measure QA impact.

Success criteria (internal priority):
1) Unit cost reduction target: 30% (hard requirement for finance sign-off).
2) Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for chat.
3) No more than 1–2% degradation on our automated QA pass rate.

We’re fine with the proposed deep-dive. Thu 2/26 10:00 PT works for our infra lead (Sana) and me. I’ll RSVP once you send the calendar invite.

Thanks — Jack
Jack Reynolds
Head of ML, FinBot Inc.
jack.reynolds@finbot.ai

Perfect — thanks Jack. I’ve booked Thu 2/26 10:00–11:00 PT for the technical deep-dive (calendar invite link in related links). Ben will lead the benchmark scope and we’ll ask Rishi to support with quantization test plans.

Immediate asks for your team before the deep-dive:
- Please fill the attached redwood_inference_cost_model.xlsx with current QPS, avg tokens, current batch size, and any monthly cost breakdowns you have. Even ballpark numbers help.
- Optional: drop a 200–400-line sample of anonymized prompts (Sana can share a redacted S3 link) so we can validate token distribution.

What our pilot will include (high-level):
- Side-by-side throughput & latency benchmark on a 1-week window using a representative workload.
- Quantized model runs (int8 and 4-bit) against your eval set to measure QA delta.
- Recommendations on batching/caching configuration (dynamic batching thresholds, KV/prefix caching for sessions).

I’ll attach a brief benchmark plan to the invite and Ben will follow up with the runbook. If anything changes on timing, let me know and we can pivot.

Best —
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.in>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.in>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: FinBot prep — benchmarking & quantization plan

Ben / Rishi — quick internal note after FinBot confirmed the deep-dive for Thu 10am PT. Key points to prepare: 

1) Benchmarks to prepare:
- Throughput profile: replicate 450 qps peak and ramp to projected 60k DAU pattern.
- Latency targets: track p50/p95/p99; target p95 <= 200ms.
- Cost model: use their token distribution (avg in/out) and our cost-per-token assumptions to produce a delta estimate for int8 and 4-bit runs.

2) Quantization plan:
- Start with int8 baseline then 4-bit where feasible. Capture inference latency, mem footprint, and QA delta on their eval set.
- Add a control A/B with unquantized model to measure QA impact precisely.

3) Deliverables for Thu:
- One-pager benchmark runbook (what we’ll run, metrics we’ll collect).
- Pre-filled cost-model template with our assumptions and placeholders for their numbers.

Ben — can you lead runbook and initial cost estimates? Rishi — please sketch the quantization test matrix (models/quant levels/expected tradeoffs).

Thanks — I’ll run the call and handle introductions.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
